beats.primary: When too many hands are pulling your life in different directions — advice, expectations, your own competing fears — this is the Name for the one grip underneath all of it that was never divided.

beats.label: catalog id 73 english verbatim
beats.primary: The One
Before the argument, the challenge: "Or have they taken for themselves gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?" — rivals with no power to do the one thing that would matter.
Then the demonstration itself: "Had there been within them [i.e., the heavens and earth] gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined."
So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
…And Allah has said, 'Do not take for yourselves two deities. He [i.e., Allah] is but one God…'
O One, O Uniquely One, gather my scattered self and unify my purpose for You.
beats.arabic: يَا وَاحِدُ يَا أَحَدُ اجْمَعْ شَمْلِي وَوَحِّدْ قَصْدِي لَكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Wahidu Ya Ahad, ijma' shamli wa wahhid qasdi lak

beats.primary: If there had been a second, the world you're standing in would not have held together. It did. Whatever is holding your life together right now is not divided between rivals — it answers to One. Al-Ahad — the second Name of your answer — is why that One has no equal to be compared against.

Where in your life right now do you keep negotiating with something as if it had a real vote? What would this week look like if you stopped treating it like a rival for control, and let it be what it actually is — nothing?

beats.primary: You have been holding a situation together by attention alone, as though letting go of it would let it fall.

beats.label: catalog id 83 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Governor
Allah says: "Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne…"
…arranging the matter [of His creation].
One phrase, present tense, with no object named. Not arranged, once, long ago. Arranging — continuously, all of it, now, including the part you are lying awake about.
…And there is not for them besides Him any patron.
O Governor, be my protector when the world drifts away. Guard me with the grip that never slips and guide me gently through what I do not understand.
beats.arabic: يَا وَالِي كُنْ لِي وَلِيًّا حِينَ يَبْتَعِدُ الدُّنْيَا عَنِّي وَتَوَلَّ أَمْرِي كُلَّهُ
beats.transliteration: Ya Wali, kun li waliyyan hina yabtab'idud-dunya 'anni wa-tawalla amri kullahu

beats.primary: Al-Waliyy is the ally who is on your side. Al-Wali is the One running the place, and the difference matters at three in the morning: you are not asking to be defended. You are asking whether anybody is at the controls.
What are you supervising tonight that is already being administered?

beats.primary: Something is already working in your favour tonight, in a place you have not thought to look. That is not a guess about your circumstances — it is the shape of a sentence the Prophet ﷺ taught a young companion, word for word.

beats.label: catalog id 96 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Benefiter

Ibn ʿAbbās, a young companion, was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ one day. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Young man, I will teach you some words: be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him in front of you."
When you ask, ask Allah. And when you seek help, seek help from Allah.

And know: if the whole creation gathered together to benefit you with something, they could not benefit you except with something Allah had already written for you. And if they gathered to harm you with something, they could not harm you except with something Allah had already written against you. The pens are lifted, and the pages are dry.
…and the [great] ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the heavens of rain, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness…
O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, pure provision, and accepted deeds.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا
beats.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an wa rizqan tayyiban wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan

beats.primary: Every person who has ever wanted to help you was still limited to what was already written for you to receive. That is not a small circle of people. It is the entire creation, and it was never enough on its own — and it was never the whole story either.
Whose help have you been waiting on tonight? Notice how small a part of the story their yes or no actually is.

beats.primary: You cannot see where this is going, and you have begun to suspect that means it is not going anywhere.

beats.label: catalog id 99 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Guide to Right Path
Allah says: "…but Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it pleasing in your hearts…"
…and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided.

Read what He actually did. Not a sign put in front of you — three changes made inside you: what you love, what looks beautiful to you, what you cannot stomach. The guidance is not a direction you were shown. It is a taste you were given.
It guides to the right course…
O Guide to the Right Path, inspire my guidance and protect me from the evil of my own self.
beats.arabic: يَا رَشِيدُ أَلْهِمْنِي رُشْدِي وَقِنِي شَرَّ نَفْسِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Rasheed, alhimni rushdi wa qini sharra nafsi

beats.primary: Al-Hadi shows you the way and you walk it. Ar-Rasheed is the arrangement you never see — the sun moved while they slept. Not being able to see where this goes is not evidence that nobody is steering it.
What has already been arranged around you that you were not awake for?

beats.primary: You have been waiting so long that you have started to read the waiting itself as the answer.

beats.label: catalog id 32 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Patient
Allah says: "He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day…"
"…the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count." Of those which you count. The sentence stops to name whose clock is being used, and it is not His.
Notice that nothing in it is late. A matter goes down, is arranged, comes back up — on time, at full speed, on a scale where a thousand of your years is one of His days.
…And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count.
O Allah, I ask You for patience and I seek refuge in You from anxiety and distress.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الصَّبْرَ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْجَزَعِ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'alukas-sabra wa a'udhu bika minal-jaza'

beats.primary: Al-Haleem is restraint: power held back from what it could rightly do. As-Sabur is not restraint at all — it is scale. He is not withholding from you. He is not on your clock, and the silence you have been reading as refusal is a matter still ascending.
How long have you actually been waiting? Put the number next to the one in the verse.

beats.primary: The part of it nobody else was there for is the part you have started to doubt yourself.

beats.label: catalog id 60 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Witness
Allah says of what He revealed: "But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge…"
Not that He knows it. That He testifies to it. The verb is the one used in a court, and the One using it is Allah.
"…and the angels bear witness as well. And sufficient is Allah as Witness." Sufficient — the testimony does not need a second signature.
…And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
O All-Seeing, You see what no one else sees. Bear witness for me in what only You know.
beats.arabic: يَا بَصِيرُ أَنْتَ تَرَى مَا لَا يَرَى أَحَدٌ فَاشْهَدْ لِي بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُهُ سِوَاكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Basir, anta tara ma la yara ahad, fashhadli bima la ya'lamuhu siwak

beats.primary: Al-Baseer sees it. Ar-Raqeeb watches it. Ash-Shaheed is the One who will say what He saw. That distinction is the whole reason this Name's duʿā asks Him not to look but to speak — and it is why the thing no one else attended still has a witness who can be called.
What is the thing no one was there for? You are not the only one who knows it happened.

beats.primary: You have done things whose cost nobody could see. That is the part you assume did not count.

beats.label: catalog id 28 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Most Appreciative
Allah describes people who give "secretly and publicly", and says they can expect "a transaction that will never perish" —
That He may give them in full their rewards and increase for them of His bounty.
Read the order. In full — and then increased. The full amount was already everything that was owed. The increase is not payment. It is appreciation.
…Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.
O Most Appreciative, appreciate my striving and do not abandon me.
beats.arabic: يَا شَكُورُ اشْكُرْ لِي سَعْيِي وَلَا تَخْذُلْنِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Shakuru ushkur li sa'yi wa la takhdhulni

beats.primary: Al-Kareem gives before you ask. Ash-Shakur answers what you already did, and answers it out of proportion. The word in the verse is not a reward; it is a Name. The smallness of what you managed is not something He is politely overlooking.
What did you do that cost you something no one else could see?

beats.primary: In the middle of your ordinary day, you are standing inside an answer you don't know you're seeing yet. This is the Name for what is already manifest, waiting for you to catch up.

beats.label: catalog id 81 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Manifest
Allah says: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them — it is the truth."
He shows signs in what you see: the ordered sky, the turning earth, the architecture of a living thing. But the Qur'an says He is also showing signs in you.

The signs in your own self — the conscience that accuses you, the mercy you cannot explain, the reason you cannot ignore — these are His speech. He keeps showing until the moment you know: *this is true.
…and the Manifest…
beats.source: Qur'an 57:3 (one word of a four-Name clause)

beats.primary: You are Al-Dhahir — there is nothing above You. You are Al-Batin — there is nothing closer to me than You.
beats.arabic: أَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَيْءٌ
beats.transliteration: Anta al-Dhahiru fa-laysa fawqaka shay', wa anta al-Batinu fa-laysa dunaka shay'

beats.primary: Az-Zahir is not a Name for knowledge you achieve. It is a Name for what is *already laid out in front of you — in every direction outside, and in the deepest part inside — and you have not seen it yet only because you have not looked. He is the One who keeps showing. You have only to receive.
Name one thing you saw today and walked past without stopping. What would change if you let yourself believe it was addressed to you?

sources.claim: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth" (beats 3–4, primary carrier)
sources.verified: ✅ `سَنُرِيهِمْ ءَايَـٰتِنَا فِى ٱلْـَٔافَاقِ وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ` — Allah's own first-person speech (`سَنُرِيهِمْ`, finite verb, grammatical subject Allah), demonstrating manifestness as an unfolding act of revelation. Spans two beats; beat 3 opens the promise, beat 4 specifies the dual location (horizons and self). No truncation

beats.primary: You want to be near something vast without being flattened by it. Those two do not usually arrive together.

beats.label: catalog id 89 english verbatim
beats.primary: Lord of Majesty and Bounty
Sūrat ar-Rahman asks one question again and again: which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
Then it stops asking. Its final line is not a question.
Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor." The sūrah of favours closes by naming the One who gave them — with both words at once."
Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.
O Lord of Majesty and Bounty, protect us from the Fire and grant us the nearness of Your generosity.
beats.arabic: يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ أَجِرْنَا مِنَ النَّارِ

beats.primary: Al-Jaleel takes the first word of this phrase from an earlier āyah. This Name is the phrase entire, and the conjunction is the point. Majesty by itself would be a reason to keep back. Honour by itself would be warmth without weight. The Qur'an never separates them, and neither does the Name.
Where have you been choosing between being safe and being close?

beats.primary: Everything you call yours arrived, and will leave. That is not a threat being made to you. It is how the ownership was always arranged.

beats.label: catalog id 88 english verbatim
beats.primary: Owner of Sovereignty
Allah opens the sūrah: "Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allah."
Every single thing named there is doing something — exalting, running, existing. Not one of them is described as owning anything.
The owning is stated separately, in its own clause, with one holder. Your grip on what you have is real. It is also a loan you are administering.
…To Him belongs dominion…
O Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and take it from whom You will. Teach me that nothing I hold is truly mine.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma Malikal-Mulk, tu'til-mulka man tasha' wa tanzi'ul-mulka mimman tasha'

beats.primary: Al-Malik is the King — the One who rules. Malik-ul-Mulk is narrower: not the ruler of a kingdom but the owner of kingship itself, including whatever share of it you are currently holding and afraid to lose.
Name the thing you are most afraid of losing. On whose account is it actually held?
